messages:
maria: Quick postmortem from the continuous scheduler rollout yesterday — small requests (seq < 32) saw a p50 regressed ~20ms and p99 jitter increased. Not catastrophic but visible on tenant dashboards. Anyone see obvious suspects?

raj: I saw the traces — looks correlated with coalesce delay spikes when global batch occupancy hits 4-8. Could be the new soft-lease handoff we merged.

devon: Yup. The soft-lease path introduces a short linear scan to find compatible microwindows, added ~6-12ms under contention. Works great for packing but hurts tiny fastpath.

maria: Right. Our assumption in the RFC was that tiny requests would rarely hit contended GPUs. Reality: a ton of low-QPS interactive requests share pools.

raj: Two options I sketched: (1) add a dedicated tiny-fastpath queue (single-slot, non-coalescing) for seq<32 + tokens<128, or (2) make soft-lease scan opportunistic with an immediate fallback to a preemptible fastpath.

sasha: Option 1 seems simpler to reason about (isolation), but it increases fragmentation of the scheduler and risk of starvation for tiny queue under bursts. Option 2 keeps consolidation but complicates the admission contract.

devon: For option 2 we could expose a thin admission API: tryAcquire(key, deadline_ms) -> {ok, lease_id} and if not ok within Xms we route to fastpath. That keeps interface small.

maria: Could we gate that behind a boolean flag per pool so Dedicated customers can opt in? We should avoid global behavior flips.

raj: Agree. Also want metrics: measure "fastpath_hit_rate", "softlease_scan_time_ms" and per-tenant "tiny_queue_wait_ms". Without these it's hard to validate.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout aborted at 18:22 UTC — automated rollback due to p50 latency threshold breach (>15ms) on canary pool-7.

maria: Ok rollback confirmed. Immediate short-term patch: bump soft-lease scan short-circuit to 0ms for requests matching tiny-fastpath heuristic. I can ship that if no objections.

devon: Ship it. Add log marker "softlease_shortcircuit=true" so we can filter.

sasha: Also propose an experiment plan: 1) Add metrics (raj) 2) Implement opportunistic short-circuit (devon) 3) Run canary with tiny-queue enabled on 10% pools (maria) 4) Observe per-tenant regressions for 48h 5) Decide on long-term: dedicated tiny queue vs opportunistic path.

raj: I'll add the metrics to the runtime telemetry library today. Names: runtime.batcher.softlease.scan_ms, runtime.batcher.fastpath_fallback_count, runtime.queue.tiny.wait_ms.

maria: We should also consider KV-cache warmup interaction: tiny requests often rely on cached KV pages; adding tiny queue may reduce cache reuse, so record kv_cache_hit_rate by queue.

devon: Good call. I'll tag cache accesses with queue_id.

raj: One more thought — backpressure: if we create a non-coalescing tiny queue we must ensure it doesn't lie about token budget to the coalescer. Otherwise coalescer will overcommit slots thinking capacity exists. Propose we surface explicit "reserved_slots" in pool descriptor.

maria: Agreed. That keeps admission contract explicit. Let's avoid implicit capacity stealing.

sasha: Action owners: raj -> telemetry & pool reserved_slots flag; devon -> opportunistic short-circuit + queue_id tag; maria -> canary config & rollout plan; I'll write the decision doc and schedule a 30-min follow-up tomorrow.

devon: Quick config snippet for the short-circuit we discussed:
```
# runtime config - tiny fastpath heuristic
fastpath: {
  enabled: true,
  max_seq: 32,
  max_tokens: 128,
  shortcircuit_scan_ms: 0,
  reserve_slots: 1
}
```

maria: Perfect. Keep logs lightweight. For the follow-up doc include perf numbers from the canary (p50/p95/p99) and the new metrics.

ops-bot: incident-bot: New follow-up scheduled: "continuous-scheduler tiny-fastpath experiment" at 2026-03-24T16:00:00Z (calendar invite sent).

raj: One last thing — long-term we may want a hybrid: tiny fastpath + micro-coalesce window of 2ms to preserve some packing. But only after we have per-queue cache hit stats.

maria: Sounds good. Thanks everyone — let's treat this as RFC follow-up, capture tradeoffs clearly in the doc (isolation vs packing vs cache reuse vs admission complexity).
